_readme: Copy this file to profiles/pantry.json and edit the lines: nothing in this repository
writes that file, so a clone has none and plan.mjs then buys no breakfast and no lunch
boxes - it says so in its output rather than failing silently.
One line per staple you rebuy. cycleDays is how long a block's cycle is; qtyPerCycle is
how much you go through in that cycle. A line may name a sku you always take; run
pin-skus.mjs after mine-history.mjs and it fills the skus from your own history.
`per` says what qtyPerCycle counts, and it matters the moment the household changes:
cycle        (default) what THIS household buys per cycle - what a number measured
out of your own orders means. Days scale it; head-counts do not.
person-day   one unit per person per day: the apple that goes in a lunch box.
person-cycle one unit per person per cycle: the slice of cheese in that same box.
Head-counts come from dinners.members in your family profile (a lunch box is counted
for the child roles, breakfast for everyone, the paper block for nobody). When that
guess is wrong - adults who take a lunch box, say - set household.blockPeople in the
Every value here is invented. The quantities are the shape of the file, not advice.
After mine-history.mjs, run `node pantry.mjs --write`: it updates the evidence on each
line, computes everyNDays at 80 % of the measured purchase gap, and adds frequent
staples whose block is known. A name in `rejected` is never added again.

mining._note: Thresholds for pantry.mjs. Edit them, or the block word lists under mining.blocks, for a household with other habits.

breakfast.note: two 1 l cartons a cycle; mined, so counted for the household
500 g of porridge oats a cycle
only when the last tub was bought 25 days ago or more

kidLunchbox.note: one loaf a cycle for the box; mined, so household-sized
one pack per person who packs a box, per cycle
one piece of fruit per box per day: 8 days x 1 person = 8 pieces
a handful of baby carrots goes in the same box

snacks.note: two pouches per child per cycle; a snack is counted per person, not per household
what this household gets through a cycle, mined

household.note: the household block counts nobody: per is left out on purpose
